identity.title: Recent approaches to modulate citrinin biosynthesis in Monascus species: a review.

content.abstract: The filamentous fungi Monascus spp. are rich sources of secondary metabolites that include Monascus azaphilone pigments, monacolin K, and gamma-aminobutyric acid, making them significant in the food, nutraceutical, cosmetic and pharmaceutical industries. Despite the industrial importance of this fungus, its production of citrinin, a nephrotoxic polyketide mycotoxin, remains a major drawback and limits its commercial application. Recent research studies have shown that the mechanism that governs citrinin biosynthesis highlights the interactions between Biosynthetic Gene Clusters (BGCs), epigenetic modifications, global regulatory networks, and environmental factors. The current understanding of the molecular and epigenetic mechanisms used to mitigate citrinin production in Monascus spp. is discussed in this review. Emphasis is given on histone acetylation and deacetylation, methylation, chromatin remodeling, the velvet complex, and the modulation of toxin biosynthesis through RNA-level gene expression control. The recent advances are critically evaluated for engineering citrinin-free strains, including transcriptomics, proteomics, multi-omics, RNA interference, CRISPR/Cas genome editing, and synthetic biology. The comparative analysis of these approaches shows that integrating epigenetic engineering with advanced genome and metabolic engineering can regulate citrinin while maintaining other important metabolite yields. Combining multi-omics and artificial intelligence-guided strain design with epigenetic interventions will accelerate the development of safe, sustainable, and high-yielding Monascus-assisted bioprocesses.
